entries.name: anime.js v4
entries.what: MIT animation engine: timelines, stagger, scroll-linking, text splitting.
entries.why: Effectively an MIT-licensed GSAP, with no handover complications. It overlaps heavily with Motion, so pick one house library. You already have a fork, but it is unmodified; npm gives you everything.
entries.size: animate + stagger 14.2 KB gzip; full 42 KB.
entries.a11y: Nothing automatic. Use createScope with a reduced-motion media query.
entries.forknote: Your existing fork is unmodified and receives no upstream fixes.
entries.install: npm i animejs@4.5.0  # import subpaths: animejs/animation, animejs/utils

entries.name: AutoAnimate
entries.what: One line to animate items being added, removed or reordered.
entries.why: Cheap polish for filters, accordions and menus, and it respects reduced motion automatically. Same-page view transitions now do much of this natively.
entries.a11y: Skips animation under reduced motion by default.

entries.name: Babylon.js
entries.what: A full 3D and game engine for the web.
entries.why: No case for it on small-business sites. Worth knowing it exists.
entries.a11y: Canvas; nothing automatic.

entries.name: Basecoat
entries.what: The shadcn/ui look rebuilt in plain HTML, Tailwind and a little vanilla JavaScript.
entries.why: Gives clients the shadcn design language on WordPress or React-free Astro. Small enough to own outright, and with a single maintainer, a fork protects you if it stalls.
entries.size: JS 10.8 KB + CSS 21.9 KB gzip for every component; per-component files available.
entries.a11y: Manages aria-expanded, aria-selected and keyboard handling. No reduced-motion rules, so add one global rule.
entries.forknote: Small, framework-free, and you would adapt it into your house kit.

entries.name: Base UI
entries.what: Unstyled, accessible React primitives from the MUI team. The layer under shadcn.
entries.why: The primitive layer the React world is converging on. Use it directly for bespoke widgets such as a combobox without fighting a design system.
entries.size: Import per component; the whole package is 143.5 KB gzip.
entries.a11y: ARIA, keyboard and focus handled. Animation is yours to gate.

entries.name: Bklit UI
entries.what: Polished React chart components on visx and Motion, installed through the shadcn registry.
entries.why: The best-looking charts here, and the source lands in your repo so you can edit it. But charts have no keyboard access, it installs a visx pre-release, and its stat-card items pull in a paid, non-transferable icon set. Skip those.
entries.handover: Yes for registry code. Install with the CLI rather than copying from Studio.
entries.size: Per chart unmeasured; Motion and visx at runtime.
entries.a11y: No keyboard handling at all. Every chart needs a caption and a visually hidden data table.
entries.install: npx shadcn@4.21.1 add @bklit/<chart>  # never the stat-card items

entries.name: Chart.js
entries.what: Framework-agnostic canvas charts.
entries.why: The one chart library that works the same on Astro, React and WordPress, so the safe default while the platform is undecided.
entries.size: 66.8 KB gzip whole; register only what you use.
entries.a11y: Canvas is not accessible by default: add a role, label and fallback table. Set animation off under reduced motion.
entries.note: Its last release passes your 12-month rule only until 2026-10-13. Commits are active.

entries.name: daisyUI
entries.what: Pure-CSS component classes for Tailwind. No JavaScript.
entries.why: Works the same on Astro, Next.js and WordPress, ships zero JavaScript, and gates its own transitions behind reduced motion better than anything else checked. The safest default while your platform is undecided.
entries.handover: Yes. Keep the MIT notice in the built CSS or a third-party notices file.
entries.size: CSS only; Tailwind emits just the classes you use. Never ship the full 97.7 KB file.
entries.a11y: 140 reduced-motion guards in its CSS. It styles native elements, so ARIA on tabs and dropdowns comes from your HTML.
entries.forknote: Theme it with CSS variables instead.
entries.install: npm i -D daisyui@5.7.47  # Tailwind v4 plugin: @plugin "daisyui";

entries.name: Apache ECharts
entries.what: A heavyweight chart and map library.
entries.why: Strongest for dashboards and maps, with the best built-in screen-reader description, which is off by default. Overkill for brochure sites.
entries.handover: Yes. Keep the licence and third-party notices.
entries.size: 359 KB gzip whole; tree-shakeable via echarts/core.
entries.a11y: Turn on its aria option for auto-generated descriptions and colour-blind patterns.
entries.install: npm i echarts@6.1.0  # import from echarts/core

entries.name: Lenis
entries.what: Smooth-scroll layer over native scrolling.
entries.why: The cheapest route to the 'premium agency' scroll feel. It does not help ordinary business sites, and it intercepts mouse-wheel input, so use it only when a client asks for that feel.
entries.a11y: Only v1.3.26 and later honour reduced motion. Pin at least 1.3.26.
entries.install: npm i lenis@1.3.26  # pin >=1.3.26 for reduced motion

entries.name: Lucide
entries.what: A consistent 24px outline icon set, 1,857 icons.
entries.why: First-party packages for vanilla JS, React, Astro and static SVG, so the same set survives whichever platform wins. Hides decorative icons from screen readers by default. Recommended default.
entries.lic: ISC, plus MIT for Feather-derived icons
entries.handover: Yes. Keep both notices in a third-party notices file.
entries.size: About 0.4 KB per icon in React; 0 KB in Astro.
entries.a11y: aria-hidden by default unless you give it a label.

entries.name: Magic UI (free)
entries.what: Copy-paste animated marketing components in React, Tailwind and Motion.
entries.why: Genuinely MIT hero and landing-page polish that clients notice. Only 5 of 79 components handle reduced motion, so each one needs a retrofit before it meets your bar.
entries.handover: Yes for the free components. Keep Magic UI Pro code out.
entries.size: Copy-paste; Motion is the main runtime.
entries.a11y: Wrap the app in MotionConfig reducedMotion="user" and guard canvas effects.
entries.cost: Low to add, Medium to make compliant
entries.forknote: Copy single components into your own registry.

entries.name: Motion
entries.what: Animation library with a framework-free JS API plus React components. Formerly Framer Motion.
entries.why: The only candidate that is first-class both without React and in React, so one skill set covers every platform you are considering. Tiny subsets: inView 0.4 KB, mini animate 3.8 KB. Use it when CSS cannot do the job.
entries.handover: Yes. Keep the MIT notice. Motion+ is a separate paid product.
entries.size: inView 0.4 KB; animate + stagger + inView + scroll 22.5 KB gzip.
entries.a11y: Plain JS has no automatic reduced-motion check; gate with matchMedia. In React set MotionConfig reducedMotion="user".
entries.note: Recommended as your one house JavaScript animation library.

entries.name: Number Flow
entries.what: Animated number transitions: digits roll for stats, prices and counters.
entries.why: The stats row ('25 years, 1,200 clients') appears on many business sites, and this does it accessibly in about 5 KB. Screen readers hear the final number, not rolling digits.
entries.a11y: Respects reduced motion by default and exposes the formatted value as its accessible name.
entries.note: Only animate real numbers. A counter invites inventing statistics.

entries.name: React Three Fiber + drei
entries.what: A React renderer for three.js, plus drei's ready-made helpers.
entries.why: Only if React wins and a project has a real 3D brief. It then cuts build time well below plain three.js.
entries.size: 55.7 KB gzip on top of three.js.
entries.a11y: As three.js.

entries.name: React Aria Components
entries.what: Adobe's accessibility-first React hooks and components.
entries.why: The strongest choice for complex, form-heavy builds: date pickers, comboboxes, multilingual and right-to-left sites. More than a brochure site needs.
entries.handover: Yes. Ship the Apache text, keep NOTICE.txt, and mark files you change.
entries.a11y: Tested across devices and assistive tech; 30+ languages.

entries.name: shadcn/ui
entries.what: A CLI that copies styled React and Tailwind components into your project. Built on Base UI by default since July 2026.
entries.why: The fastest route to a consistent kit you own on React or Next.js. Private registries let your reusable pieces install into each client repo, which fits your licensing model. Little use on Astro without React islands, none on WordPress.
entries.handover: Yes. Copied files carry no header, so add the MIT notice to a third-party notices file. Its class-variance-authority dependency is Apache-2.0.
entries.size: Copy-paste, no runtime package. Runtime: Base UI, class-variance-authority, lucide-react.
entries.a11y: ARIA and keyboard come from Base UI. No reduced-motion handling; add a global rule.
entries.cost: Low on React, Medium on Astro
entries.forknote: The CLI already gives you source you own.
entries.note: class-variance-authority last released 2024-11-26, which fails your 12-month rule. Vendor it or grant an exception.
entries.install: npx shadcn@4.21.1 init  # in an Astro project with @astrojs/react

entries.name: Tabler Icons
entries.what: A large MIT icon set, 6,220 icons, outline and filled.
entries.why: The fallback when Lucide lacks an industry-specific icon. Same 24px, 2px-stroke grid, so the two mix cleanly.
entries.a11y: Add aria-hidden yourself on decorative icons.

entries.name: three.js
entries.what: The standard WebGL 3D engine.
entries.why: Nearly every other 3D option runs on it, so it is worth understanding. A custom scene is rarely justified on a fixed-price site: about 180 KB gzip and weeks of work at your hours.
entries.a11y: Canvas content is invisible to screen readers; stop the render loop under reduced motion.
entries.forknote: Far too large to maintain a fork.

entries.name: visx
entries.what: Airbnb's low-level D3 and React chart primitives.
entries.why: The foundation under Bklit. Building charts from primitives costs too many hours for fixed-price work.
entries.size: Modular; a shape module is 10.5 KB gzip.
entries.a11y: None built in.

entries.name: Aceternity UI (free)
entries.what: Animated React components served from a website registry, with no public repo.
entries.why: Good for visual ideas. Its licence forbids redistributing source files, which collides with handing a client their repo. Study the effects and rebuild them with Motion.
entries.handover: Risky: a client repo containing the source is arguably redistribution.
entries.a11y: 1 of 12 sampled components handles reduced motion.
entries.forknote: Nothing to fork, and the licence forbids redistribution.
entries.use_note: Licence forbids redistributing source files; rebuild effects with Motion.

entries.name: astro-icon (Iconify)
entries.what: Build-time icon inlining for Astro from 238 icon sets. No client JavaScript.
entries.why: One component for Lucide, Tabler and others on Astro. The trap: each set carries its own licence, and about 70 of the 238 need attribution, are copyleft or non-commercial. Use an allow-list.
entries.lic: MIT (tool); each icon set has its own
entries.handover: Yes for the tool. Record the licence of each set used.
entries.a11y: Set aria-hidden on decorative icons.
entries.note: Core if Astro wins. Avoid @iconify/react, last released 2025-09-15.

entries.name: Astro view transitions
entries.what: Astro's built-in router: app-like navigation with view transitions and fallbacks.
entries.why: Podium-style page transitions on Astro with accessibility handled for you. It switches animation off under reduced motion, announces page changes, and can keep a video playing across pages.
entries.a11y: Disables view-transition animation under reduced motion and announces route changes.
entries.cost: Low to Medium; scripts must re-run on astro:page-load
entries.install: built into astro: import { ClientRouter } from 'astro:transitions'

entries.name: Origin UI / coss
entries.what: Hundreds of copy-paste form and app components, kept as a legacy snapshot inside the coss repo.
entries.why: A big library of patterns to study. The repo's root licence is AGPL. Only the apps/origin and apps/ui folders are MIT, so copy from those and never fork the whole repo.
entries.lic: MIT in two folders; AGPL-3.0 elsewhere
entries.handover: Only code copied from the MIT folders, with the notice.
entries.size: Copy-paste; runtime is a pinned Radix release candidate.
entries.a11y: Inherits Radix; reduced motion not verified.
entries.forknote: Forking the repo pulls in AGPL code.
entries.use_note: Root licence is AGPL; only apps/origin and apps/ui are MIT. Study patterns only.

entries.name: CSS animated background
entries.what: Two to four blurred radial-gradient shapes moved with CSS transforms. No JavaScript.
entries.why: Gives most clients the 'alive' hero they want for under 1 KB of CSS and about 1 to 2 hours, with no WebGL cost at all. Try this before any shader library.
entries.a11y: Wrap the animation in a no-preference reduced-motion query.

entries.name: CSS scroll-driven animations
entries.what: CSS keyframes driven by scroll position or by an element moving through the viewport. No JavaScript.
entries.why: Replaces most of what people install ScrollTrigger or AOS for: scrubbed reveals, parallax, progress bars. 0 KB and no main-thread cost. Podium already uses it for its hero parallax.
entries.handover: Nothing to retain; it is the client's own CSS.
entries.a11y: A reduced-motion media query stops it completely. Gate with @supports so Firefox, which lacks it, gets static content.
entries.forknote: A browser feature; nothing to fork.

entries.name: dotLottie player
entries.what: Maintained Lottie animation player using a WASM engine.
entries.why: For illustrated or mascot animations a client already owns as Lottie files. Heavy, so lazy-load below the fold and self-host the WASM. A short muted video is often cheaper.
entries.handover: Yes. The animation files are plain data the client keeps.
entries.a11y: No reduced-motion logic; don't autoplay under reduce.

entries.name: Embla Carousel
entries.what: Small, dependency-free carousel engine; you supply markup and styles.
entries.why: The best carousel when a client insists on one. Push back first: a CSS scroll-snap row needs no JavaScript.
entries.a11y: v9 adds an accessibility plugin. Never autoplay without a visible pause control.
entries.note: Stable 8.6.0 (2025-04-04) fails the 12-month rule, and 9.0 has been a release candidate since January 2026. Do not ship a pre-release to a client who owns it. Use the CSS scroll-snap row until 9.0 stable ships (library-scout, 2026-10-01).
entries.install: do not install yet: 8.6.0 fails the 12-month rule and 9.0 is still a release candidate; use the scroll-snap row (patterns.md 12)

entries.name: GSAP
entries.what: The most capable JS animation platform: timelines, ScrollTrigger, SplitText, Flip, MorphSVG. Every plugin is now free.
entries.why: The fastest way to build Podium-level work for a rare premium client, and SplitText is the most accessible text splitter available. For ordinary business sites CSS covers most of it, and the licence complicates your handover.
entries.handover: The client holds it directly under Webflow's terms. Your contract must carve GSAP out of the 'modify, sublicense, transfer' clause. Keep every @license header.
entries.size: Core 27 KB; with ScrollTrigger 44.2 KB gzip.
entries.a11y: Nothing automatic; use gsap.matchMedia. ScrollSmoother ignores reduced motion entirely.
entries.forknote: The licence grants use only. There is no right to modify or redistribute, and the repo has no LICENSE file.
entries.note: Not open source. Banned in no-code animation tools that compete with Webflow; Webflow may amend or terminate the terms.
entries.install: npm i gsap@3.15.0  # flagged licence: carve out of client sublicensing

entries.name: Headless UI
entries.what: Tailwind Labs' small set of unstyled, accessible components.
entries.why: Not much now. shadcn on Base UI covers more, and the Vue package fails your 12-month rule.
entries.a11y: ARIA and keyboard handled.

entries.name: Iconoir
entries.what: An MIT outline set with a lighter 1.5px stroke, 1,671 icons.
entries.why: For a client whose brand wants finer lines. Not needed if Lucide and Tabler cover the job.
entries.a11y: No default aria-hidden.

entries.name: Locomotive Scroll v5
entries.what: Lenis plus data-scroll attributes for reveals and parallax.
entries.why: Lenis plus CSS scroll-driven animation does the same with less code, and v5 locks you to Lenis 1.3.17, which ignores reduced motion.
entries.a11y: Parallax runs regardless of reduced motion.
entries.forknote: Study its progress-variable pattern; don't ship it.
entries.use_note: Pins Lenis 1.3.17, which ignores reduced motion. Use Lenis + CSS scroll-driven animation.

entries.name: <model-viewer>
entries.what: A web component that shows a 3D product model the visitor can turn around.
entries.why: The one 3D feature a small business might genuinely need: a product buyers want to inspect. One HTML tag on any platform; most of the cost is preparing the model, not the code.
entries.size: About 284 KB gzip with three.js; load on click behind a poster image.
entries.a11y: Its alt text becomes the accessible name. Don't enable auto-rotate.

entries.name: Motion Primitives
entries.what: 33 copy-paste React and Motion animation components.
entries.why: The cleanest genuinely MIT animation set. Components are small and mostly depend only on Motion, so they are easier to keep fast than Magic UI. None handle reduced motion on their own.
entries.a11y: 0 of 33 handle reduced motion; MotionConfig reducedMotion="user" is mandatory.
entries.install: copy components from motion-primitives.com; runtime: motion@13.5.0

entries.name: Radix Primitives
entries.what: Unstyled, accessible React primitives.
entries.why: Stable and behind a lot of existing code, but shadcn moved its default to Base UI in July 2026. Mostly useful when maintaining Radix-based code.
entries.a11y: ARIA, focus and keyboard handled.

entries.name: React Bits
entries.what: 213 animated React components, many of them WebGL.
entries.why: Visually impressive, but 'MIT + Commons Clause' forbids sublicensing the components, so they cannot go into your reusable kit. Many effects pull in GSAP, three.js or the stale OGL.
entries.handover: A finished site, yes. Your reusable kit, no.
entries.a11y: 68 of 213 handle reduced motion.
entries.forknote: The licence forbids redistributing the components.
entries.use_note: MIT + Commons Clause forbids sublicensing; cannot enter client repos or the kit.

entries.name: View Transitions API
entries.what: Browser-native animated transitions between page states and between pages.
entries.why: Two lines of CSS give a static multi-page site page transitions without a router, the job Barba and Swup used to do. Browsers without support just navigate normally.
entries.a11y: Browsers do not switch it off for reduced motion. You add one CSS rule.
entries.cost: Low for a fade, Medium for shared-element morphs

entries.name: Swiper
entries.what: Touch slider and carousel with autoplay, pagination and a Web Component build; no dependencies.
entries.why: Stable, MIT and actively released, with an accessibility module on by default. The heaviest carousel checked: about 25 KB gzip with autoplay, a11y and navigation is 84% of the 30 KB page budget. Use it only when a brief needs looping, thumbnails or effects that a CSS scroll-snap row cannot do. It ships no pause control, so you must build one.
entries.size: 20.8 KB gzip core; 25.3 KB with Autoplay, A11y and Navigation (measured with esbuild); CSS about 2 KB gzip.
entries.a11y: No reduced-motion handling and no pause control anywhere in the package; autoplay does not pause on keyboard focus. Import Autoplay only when matchMedia allows motion, set speed to 0 under reduce, and add your own visible pause button (patterns.md pattern 6). The a11y module is on by default: labelled slides, buttons with Enter and Space.
entries.note: Approved by the operator 2026-10-01 after a library-scout check. Single maintainer; 9 stable releases since 2026-06-26 including a new major, so pin exactly and re-test before bumping. The loop-mode keyboard-trap fix only landed in 14.3.0.
entries.install: npm i --save-exact swiper@14.3.0  # import Autoplay only behind the reduced-motion gate; build your own pause button

entries.name: Accessible Astro Components
entries.what: 24 zero-dependency Astro components: skip link, modal, tabs, accordion, form validation, reduced-motion toggle.
entries.why: Serves your WCAG 2.2 AA floor directly with near-zero JavaScript. A natural accessibility layer under Starwind or daisyUI.
entries.a11y: Built to WCAG and ARIA practice per component; ships a reduced-motion toggle that respects the system setting.
entries.forknote: Small, no dependencies, and you would restyle it into your house kit.
entries.use_note: Added because the Astro starter uses it (approved in the 2026-10-01 plan). The operator may veto.
